title: Selling Partner API (SP-API) | Sell on Amazon
snippet:
With Selling Partner API (SP-API), you can build automated solutions for your own sales in the Amazon store. Or you can create and list apps for other Amazon sellers in the [Selling Partner Appstore](https://sell.amazon.com/tools/selling-partner-appstore).

[Selling Partner API (SP-API)](https://developer.amazonservices.com/) is a REST-based API that helps Amazon sellers and vendors programmatically access their data for orders, shipments, payments, and much more. You can integrate automated solutions just for your business, or use SP-API to integrate and list apps in the [Selling Partner Appstore](https://sell.amazon.com/tools/selling-partner-appstore) for use by other Amazon sellers.

Adjust prices automatically to keep offers competitive and help increase sales.

Do I need a Professional selling account to create an SP-API developer profile?
Yes, only Professional selling accounts can access Developer Central and integrate with SP-API. If you have an Individual selling account, you can [upgrade at any time](https://sellercentral.amazon.com/help/hub/reference/external/G201747610). For more information, visit [our documentation website](https://developer-docs.amazon.com/sp-api/docs/registering-as-a-developer).

*A Professional selling account is $39.99/month + selling fees. [Learn more](https://sell.amazon.com/pricing#selling-plans)

title: Amazon Selling Partner API: what it takes to get access
snippet:
**TL;DR:** The Amazon Selling Partner API is Amazon's developer interface for reading and managing seller and vendor data. Private seller apps need a professional selling account and a developer profile that Amazon reviews, with roles picked from 17 options. Every call then runs inside per-operation rate limits. Commerce Spine already carries Amazon's approval and gives your own agent a read-only API, starting with a free plan on one account.

A seller with a professional selling account can register, and only the primary account user can complete it. Individual selling accounts are not eligible for private seller applications, though Amazon lets you upgrade to a professional plan at any time. [amz-registration]
Public developers carry extra requirements. Their website must meet Amazon's guidelines for public developers and service providers, and their app has to appear in the Appstore under the Solution Provider Portal Agreement. Both public and private applications also face authorization limits. [amz-registration]
## How do you register as an SP-API developer?
You register by filling in a Developer Profile from Seller Central, under Apps and Services and then Develop Apps. The form asks for contact information, the data you need, the roles that apply to you, your use cases and your security controls. You then accept the Solution Provider Portal Agreement, the Acceptable Use Policy and the Data Protection Policy, and choose Register. [amz-register]
Amazon asks you to keep the profile under 500 words and to write it yourself instead of copying its policies. The team that owns data security should answer the security questions. Amazon then opens a case with next steps. If it asks for more information, you have five days to respond before the case closes and your access stays unchanged. [amz-registration] [amz-register]

Roles decide which operations your application may call, and a call without the right role returns a 403 error. Amazon's [roles page](https://developer-docs.amazon.com/sp-api/docs/roles-in-the-selling-partner-api) lists 17 roles. All 17 are open to sellers and 6 are open to vendors. Another 4 carry the Restricted label because they touch personal data, so they need extra detail on data use and security. [amz-roles]

Each SP-API operation has its own rate limit and burst limit, enforced with a token bucket. Every request spends a token and Amazon refills the bucket at a set rate per second. A request that finds the bucket empty is throttled

title: FAQs for Selling Partner API for Vendors
snippet:
Is there an additional price for adopting Vendor APIs?
No, it is a free service and you can start Vendor API integration by [registering as a developer.](https://github.com/amzn/selling-partner-api-docs/blob/main/guides/en-US/developer-guide/SellingPartnerApiDeveloperGuideForVendors.md#registering-as-a-developer)
Note: To register as a developer, you will need to create an Amazon Web Service (AWS) account.
- Identity and Access Management (IAM) is a feature offered at no additional charge.
- If you sign up for the free tier and the only AWS service you use is IAM, your account should continue to be free. You might incur charges after 12 months for the use of other AWS services by your users, if you use any other AWS services.
- You can reference the [IAM Pricing FAQ](https://aws.amazon.com/iam/faqs/?nc=sn&loc=5#Pricing) and the [AWS Free tier info](https://aws.amazon.com/free/) which includes information about which services always have free usage tiers or limits and which ones have 12 month free trials.

How do I get an access token for the API requests? A Login with Amazon (LWA) access token authorizes your application to take certain actions on behalf of a selling partner. An access token expires one hour after it is issued, and must be included with every request to the Selling Partner API.
For more information, see the [Connecting to the Selling Partner API](https://github.com/amzn/selling-partner-api-docs/blob/main/guides/en-US/developer-guide/SellingPartnerApiDeveloperGuideForVendors.md#connecting-to-the-selling-partner-api) within the Selling Partner Developer Guide for Vendors.

title: Getting started for private developers
snippet: Before creating a private application, you must first be registered as an Amazon Seller using [Amazon Seller Central](https://sellercentral.amazon.com/?ld=NSGoogle&pageName=US%3ASPDS%3ASPAPI-private-developer). Only Professional Selling Accounts can register to develop or integrate with Selling Partner API. Individual accounts are not eligible. You can upgrade your account to a professional plan at any time.

title: Amazon Seller Central API Guide (2026)
snippet:
Amazon has no product called the Seller Central API. When people search for one they mean the Selling Partner API (SP-API), the REST API through which software reads and changes what a seller otherwise handles in Seller Central: orders, listings, inventory, reports, payments and shipments. Advertising is not part of it. Campaigns and ad performance live in the separate Amazon Ads API. A third name that turns up in searches, the Product Advertising API, was an affiliate product and is now deprecated; it never gave access to a seller account.

You do not get API keys from a settings page. Access is a sequence:
1. **Register as a developer.** A seller building for its own company fills in the Developer Profile in Seller Central under Apps and Services, Develop Apps, describing its data use and security controls. Amazon reviews it and opens a case.
2. **Request roles.** A role is permission for a group of operations and data: Product Listing, Pricing, Inventory and Order Tracking, Amazon Fulfillment, Finance and Accounting, Brand Analytics and others. Calling an operation without its role returns `403`.
3. **Register the application** and select, from your approved roles, the ones it uses.
4. **Authorize it** for a selling account, which yields a refresh token.
5. **Call the regional endpoint** with a short-lived Login with Amazon access token.

**Restricted data.** Roles that expose buyer names, addresses or tax data are marked restricted: Direct-to-Consumer Shipping, Tax Invoicing, Tax Remittance, Professional Services and Selling Partner Support. They require more detail on data handling, and for public developers Amazon describes an architecture review with its solutions architects.

In late 2025 Amazon announced fees for third-party developers, an annual subscription plus monthly usage fees tied to the number of GET calls, to begin in 2026. We described that plan in [our article on SP-API fees and call optimization](https://deltologic.com/blog/amazon-sp-api-2026-fees-how-to-optimize-your-api-calls-and-save-money). It did not go ahead. Amazon's [announcement page](https://developer.amazonservices.com/announcement-new-tier-advanced-solution-provider-portal) is now headed as a cancellation of the third-party developer fees and states that Amazon "will not move forward with the SP-API usage and annual fees at this time".

title: Amazon Seller Data Access
snippet:
Sellers that have a professional selling account and authorized third parties that are registered as Selling Partner API (SP-API) developers can use the SP-API to programmatically access Amazon's Seller data (also referred to as business user data), including customers' data. Through SP-API, sellers and authorized third parties have access to various tools and downloadable reports that include listings, returns, inventory, orders, product recommendations, payments, feedback, and analytics. Sellers can also access the data directly on [Seller Central](https://developer-docs.amazon.com/sp-api/docs/seller-central-urls).

You only need to register as a developer once, in any [region and store](https://developer-docs.amazon.com/sp-api/docs/marketplace-ids), to have continuous access to the SP-API. As part of registration, you must complete a Developer Profile. The Developer Profile collects the following:
- Your organization’s contact information
- Information about the data you require from Amazon Services APIs
- Security and use information (to ensure your compliance with Amazon’s [policies and agreements](https://developer-docs.amazon.com/sp-api/docs/policies-and-agreements))
- Access requirements
